examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
# main config
agents:
  coder:  # the coder agent
    $ref: file:agents/coder.yaml
    temperature: 0.2  # override

.troupe/agents/coder.yaml:
model: opus  # shared model
prompt: file:prompt.txt

results.1: All three arms: exit 3, no file changed, but the messages differ. One arm: `its whole value comes from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml; not replacing it`. One arm: `value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/coder.yaml with overrides; refusing to replace it (change a path inside it instead); no file changed`. One arm: `error: agents.coder: its whole value comes from include 'file:agents/coder.yaml' in /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml; change the included file instead`.
results.2: Exit 3, no file changed: `agents.coder: the whole value comes from the include file:agents/coder.yaml; change the included file instead`.
results.3: Both arms: exit 3, no file changed. One arm: `write refused: agents.coder: value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/coder.yaml; refusing to replace it`. One arm: `agents.coder: value comes from include .troupe/agents/coder.yaml` (no hint about what to do instead).

examples.input: `config set agents.coder "{temperature: 0.5, model: sonnet, prompt: \"Write tests.\nShip it.\n\"}" --reason multi-file`

results.1: All three arms: exit 3 with the same message each gave for the first set; no file changed.
results.2: Exit 3 with the same message as before; no file changed.
results.3: Both arms: exit 3 with the same message each gave for the first set; no file changed.

results.1: All three arms: exit 0. Only the three starting import entries are listed (model opus, the prompt text, temperature 0.2). No change or reason is recorded.
results.2: Exit 0. Only the three starting import entries are listed. No change is recorded.
results.3: Both arms: exit 0. Only the three starting import entries are listed. No change is recorded.

context.in_practice: Every implementation on every route treated replacing the whole `agents.coder` value as forbidden, because that value comes from an included file. So none of them tried to write several files, and the difference between the routes never showed up. Route 1 checks everything first and then writes the files one by one, with no rollback if a later write fails. Route 2 also writes each file safely, rolls back on failure, and names any file it could not restore. That only matters when a write fails partway through, which this test never caused. The visible differences are only in the refusal messages: some say what to do instead, and one gives no hint.
context.stakes: When one `config set` would change several files (the main config, an included agent file and a prompt file), a user needs either all of those files changed or none of them. A half-applied change leaves the config inconsistent. In this test, however, every implementation refused the set before writing anything, so the multi-file write path was never reached on any route.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 is simpler, but if the disk fails partway through a write, some files can be left changed. Route 2 adds rollback code so a failure leaves nothing changed, or names the file that couldn't be restored. Route 3 had no stated plan.

plan_why: A mapping set that touches three files (the override in troupe.yml, model in agents/coder.yaml, and the CRLF text include prompt.txt). The first attempt fails only the last file's check, so it shows whether the earlier files are left untouched (routes 1 and 2) or partly written (a route that never planned this). The second attempt succeeds and writes all three files, and history shows the events sharing one change id.
routes: Compute and verify every file first, then write each; nothing is written if any check fails
Refuse multi-file sets, reworked within step 1 to: verify all, write each atomically, roll back on failure, and name any file that could not be restored
